title: Why Web Users Scan Instead of Reading
content:
September 30, 1997 · Updated Aug. 1, 2010 2010-08-01

Sidebar to Jakob Nielsen's column on how users read on the Web.

More research is needed to truly know why 79 percent of Web users scan rather than read, but here are four plausible reasons:

Studies of Microsoft's ClearType technology show that it increases reading speeds from screens by 5%. Not nearly enough to make computer screens as good as paper, but at least it's a step forward.

Studies of iPad and Kindle reading speeds show that these tablets are still slightly slower than printed books, though much better than the old studies (discussed above) used to find for computer-based reading.
